narrative.overview:
The site is a bound atlas of one person's work. Every page is a sheet from the same atlas. The main page is the night-map cover, covered in drifting contour lines. The Career sheet is a transit route, the Algorithms sheet a blueprint, and the Games sheet a margin doodle that turned into an arcade. They share one printing: the same slate ground, the same see-through panels, the same card anatomy, header, footer and sound toggle. A sheet changes only its background, accent, heading font and card shape. The projects are what the atlas is for, so the chrome stays thin and lets them lead.

Components are **crafted instruments**. Every card has a small, precise, hand-made detail that belongs to its sheet: corner brackets and a scan line on the blueprint, grip ridges and stepped pixel corners on the cartridge, a round logo badge on the route. These details are what make the site recognisable, and they show up where a person looks, not as decoration spread across the page. Behind everything, one `<canvas>` runs a slow generative background (noise contours, a pathfinding or sorting run, a parallax starfield, a pulsing map grid). It is dimmed well back, pauses when the tab is hidden, and becomes a still frame under reduced motion.

Dark ("Night over the map") is the default, and light follows the OS setting with its own darker, readable accent values. Density is calm: one content column of at most 1120px, generous section spacing, and body text kept to about 60 characters per line.
keyCharacteristics: One shared base with themed sheets, where only theme tokens change from page to page.
One accent per sheet, and in the arcade a second one (yellow).
See-through panels floating over a live, dimmed generative canvas.
One small hand-made detail per component that belongs to its sheet.
System sans for reading, monospace for labels, data and anything "technical".
Sound and motion are opt-in or polite, never required.

rules.name: The One Ink Per Sheet Rule
rules.body: Each page has exactly one accent (the arcade has two: magenta and coin yellow). The main page is the only place where all the inks appear together, and only as the per-destination `--card-accent` on the three summits, where each ink also tints its own summit's contour rings.

rules.name: The Day Ink Rule
rules.body: Every accent has a darker day version for light mode, chosen so text stays readable. A new accent isn't finished until its day version exists and is defined in a `prefers-color-scheme: light` block.

rules.name: The Signal Is State Rule
rules.body: Signal Green means "active, pressed or running". It is never used for decoration or as a second brand colour.

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Anything that reads like data (dates, periods, counts, complexity, tags, filter labels, stats) is set in monospace. Anything that reads like prose is set in the system sans.

rules.name: The Pixel Font Stays In The Arcade Rule
rules.body: Press Start 2P appears only on the Games page and in its games. It is never used for body text, and it is used at no more than about 0.8rem outside the title.

rules.name: The Shared Chassis Rule
rules.body: Header, footer, sound toggle, container widths, gutters, breakpoints and the card structure (media, body, badges, title, summary, expanding details, actions) are identical on every sheet. A new page is a new theme on this same base, not a new layout.

rules.name: The Glow Is A Response Rule
rules.body: Panels are flat and see-through at rest. Accent-coloured light appears only for hover, focus, open or "reached". A glow that is always on means something is wrong.

rules.name: The Canvas Stays Behind Rule
rules.body: The generative background is dimmed until it cannot compete with the text (for example at 0.6 opacity on the blueprint). It never takes pointer events, pauses when the tab is hidden, and becomes a still frame under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Circle Means Identity Rule
rules.body: Circles are reserved for identity: the portrait, the JJK brand mark, company logos in station badges, person avatars and the round sound toggle. Content cards are never circular.

dos: Do theme a new page by overriding only the theme tokens (`--bg`, `--bg-glow`, `--surface`, `--line`, `--text`, `--muted`, `--accent`, `--radius`) and the heading font in its own stylesheet. Keep the shared base untouched.
Do give every new accent a day version in a `prefers-color-scheme: light` block, and check text contrast in both modes.
Do give each component one crafted detail that belongs to its sheet (brackets, ridges, badges, prompt glyphs). Put it where the visitor's attention already is.
Do set dates, counts, tags, periods and technical notes in the monospace stack.
Do keep every generative background on the single `#bg` canvas: dimmed, pointer-events off, paused when hidden, and a still frame under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do use `translate` for entrance animations (the `rise` keyframe) so they don't clash with the `transform` used on hover.
Do keep project images at 16:10 and let `data/projects.js` drive every card.
donts: Don't give a sheet a second layout, header or card structure. Page themes change tokens and details, not the base.
Don't put more than one accent on a subpage (the arcade's coin yellow is the only second accent), or use Signal Green for anything but active state.
Don't use resting shadows or always-on glows on cards. Light is a response to interaction.
Don't use Press Start 2P outside the Games page, or for body text.
Don't make content cards circular. Circles mean identity.
Don't autoplay sound, or animate anything that ignores reduced motion or hidden tabs.
Don't hide the dashed placeholder badge on made-up content, or present placeholder illustrations as real project imagery.
